key_insight: IF-MAP prioritizes agents by their estimated potential to improve end-to-end performance, rather than by responsibility for failures.
engineering_relevance: Teams can focus prompt optimization or model upgrades on promising agents instead of spending resources improving every agent.
method: Probe each agent with controlled semantic prompt perturbations and measure end-to-end loss changes.
Fit a regularized local response model in a low-dimensional prompt-embedding subspace.
Rank agents by estimated response norm without accessing model parameters or gradients.
evidence_signal: Across six workflows spanning coding, question answering, and math, prioritized prompt optimization gained 3.81 percentage points versus 1.85 for uniform selection; upgrades across five target models gained 7.62–16.42 points versus 3.81–8.62.
watch_item: Probing adds overhead, and local sensitivity to prompt perturbations may not reliably predict gains from every subsequent intervention.
paper_title: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems
